To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have calculated the angular distribution of the differential cross section for pi d to d d at 142, 180, and 256 Mev and have shown that the angular distributions of the tensor polarisation for the same reaction are sensitive to the presence of dibaryon states.

(i) the dibaryon resonant structure in the pi d system can be described in terms of a few resonances, (ii) the dibaryons are not the only contributors to the pi d scattering, and (iii) the dibaryonic contribution to the pi d system is not a dominant one.

the dibaryon resonant structure of the πd scattering amplitude is strongly constrained by the experimental data and that the angular distribution of the vector polarisation at 180 MeV is the most sensitive probe of the dibaryon structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: - the search for dibaryon resonacne signals in elastic pi d scattering at low energies, - the study of the dibaryon resonace 1D2 and its mixing with other isospin-1 dibaryons in the elastic channel pi d to pi p, - the study and comparison of the dibaryonic structure of the 1F3 dibaryon resonance with the dibaryonic structures of the 1D2 dibaryon resonance and of

the study of dibaryon resonance contributions to the Faddeev amplitude for the elastic scattering of a pion and a deuteron, and the calculation of angular distributions of cross sections, vector and tensor polarisation parameters for the reaction pi d to pi' d' at Tlabpi=142, 180, and 256 Mev.
the following questions: 1. What are the effects of dibaryons on the angular distribution of elastic πd scattering?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data do not provide a clear signal for any of the three resonances.
the experimental data do not exclude the presence of dibaryon resonance signals in the angular distributions of the polarisation observ-ables.
the dibaryon resonant contributions are very small and cannot be resolved from background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dibaryon resonant contributions to the pi d elastic cross section can be identified in the vector and tensor polarisation observables, but not in the differential cross sections.
the dibaryons 1D2 and 1G 4 can be excluded, while the 3F3 resonance can explain the experimental data.
the Faddeev approach is very promising for the study of dibaryons in πd scattering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a clear dibaryon signal is present in the vector polarisation at Tlabpi=256 MeV.
the angular distributions of polarisation observables can be used to constrain dibaryon resonant contributions in elastic pion-deuteron scattering.
the tensor polarisation T20 and the vector polarisation T21 can be used to search for dibaryon signals.
